cues.text: Pinder’s Animal Park. Hello?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Oh, hello, I’m ringing to ask whether you have any jobs available...
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Ah, what sort of work are you looking for? Is that permanent, or part time or ...
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Actually I’m just looking for temporary work. I’m a student.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Oh right. I’ll just get a form, and ask you a few questions. Then I’ll pass your application on to our recruitment section. Is that OK?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Fine, thank you.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: So, starting with your name.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: It’s Jane Lamerton.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Is that L-A-double M-E-R-T-O-N?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: There’s only one M in it.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Oh, right. And your address?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: It’s forty-two West Lane.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Right ... And is that in Exeter?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Yes.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Okay. And can you give me your mobile phone number?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Right. Now, the next thing is, when are you available to start work?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: I finish college on the eighth of June, that’s in three weeks’ time, but I can’t start work till the eleventh because I’ve got a hospital appointment on the tenth of June.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: No problem. Now I need to ask you a few questions about the type of job that might be suitable. Do you have any particular kind of work in mind? It doesn’t necessarily mean that you will get work in the field that you want, but I can record your preferences.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Well I’d do anything, and I have worked as an assistant animal keeper before, when I was still at school. But I’m studying at a catering college now, and I’d really like to get some experience as an assistant cook if possible.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Right. So that’s your first choice. Have you done that kind of job before?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: No. But I’ve helped my aunt sometimes - she runs a cafe in Exeter.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Mmm. Would you say you’ve got any relevant skills then?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Well I’m used to using the kind of equipment you usually find in a kitchen.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: OK . And I know you’re still studying, but do you already have any qualifications related to that kind of work? A hygiene qualification, for example?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: I haven’t, no, but I’ve got a certificate in food-handling. I did it before I decided to become a full-time student.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Fine. OK. That means you wouldn’t need any specific training if you did get the kind of work you wanted. But you’d have to do a short course on First Aid. All our new employees do that. It just takes half a day, and most people find it generally useful.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Oh yes, I’m sure it is.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Well that’s about it, really. Just one last thing - can you give me the name of someone who would give you a reference? Like a previous employer or ...
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Oh yes, you can put Dr Ruth Price.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: OK ... Is that one of your college lecturers?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: She’s my college tutor. She’s known me for over two years, and I’m sure she wouldn’t mind. In fact she’s given me a reference before.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Fine. We’d probably contact her by phone - do you happen to know her number?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: I’ve got it on my phone - yes - it’s 0208685114. That’s a landline.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Good. Well. As I say, I can’t promise anything, but I’ll pass your application on and you should hear in a few days. Is there anything else?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Just one thing - I suffer from a particular type of colour blindness, and sometimes employers have to make special arrangements for that.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: OK. I’ll make a note of that. It won’t be a problem, but it’s good that you’ve made us aware of it. You can provide us with more details if you are offered a job.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Okay. Thanks very much. Bye.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Bye.
cues.speaker: Man
